# Counterparty Credit Risk & CVA Engine: results summary

*Generated by `run_all.py`: valuation date 2026-10-02, 10,000 Hull-White paths × 121 dates, seed 42. Every number is read from `reports/tables`; see `docs/technical_note.md` for the methods.*

## In one sentence

A Monte Carlo counterparty-risk engine for a 10-swap interest-rate portfolio: it models future exposure under exact one-factor Hull-White rates, prices unilateral CVA from default probabilities and recovery, and measures how netting, collateral and credit and market assumptions change it.

## Project summary

- Built a Monte Carlo counterparty-credit-risk engine in Python for a 10-swap USD interest-rate portfolio: bootstrapped a US Treasury zero curve, simulated an exact one-factor Hull-White model (10,000 paths × 121 dates, martingale-tested) and priced unilateral CVA with pathwise discounting to ±0.7% Monte Carlo precision.
- Quantified counterparty-risk mitigation: legal netting cut portfolio CVA by 60% (79% for a balanced netting set vs 9% for a one-directional one), a zero-threshold CSA with a 14-day margin period removed a further 92%, and common-random-number sensitivities ranked the CVA drivers (portfolio tenor, credit spread, recovery, rate volatility).

## Limitations

- Single-curve Treasury discounting and projection; no day counts, calendars or historical fixings.
- One-factor Gaussian Hull-White with assumed (not calibrated) parameters: all rates move together and rates can go negative.
- Assumed CDS-equivalent spreads with the credit-triangle hazard λ ≈ s/(1−R); deterministic hazards independent of rates (no wrong-way risk); unilateral CVA only.
- Simplified one-way CSA: MTA added to the threshold, coupons paid during the MPoR, no initial margin or haircuts.
